findings.text: The first paragraph tells a newcomer what Athena is, who it is for, and what problem it solves. Someone who reads only that paragraph can say what the project is and why it matters.
findings.source: Header lede: "Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository... It solves the problem of AI edits that arrive unreviewed and unaccountable."

findings.text: The second section shown is an error message. It sits where the proof of Athena's main promise should be: the models, verdict and cost it records. A newcomer sees the headline feature fail before seeing it work.
findings.source: Check it on a real job: "The records of job 20261029-073603-7kqv could not be read here, so no models, verdict or costs are shown: no reading record for job 20261029-073603-7kqv."

findings.text: Athena's home page is mostly a detailed study of another tool, firstmate. A newcomer who came to learn about Athena has to work through states, transitions and 45 claims about firstmate, and nothing says why firstmate was chosen or that the study only shows what Athena can produce.
findings.source: Title and h1: "Athena explains how firstmate handles work"

findings.text: A link meant for the owner sits among the opening lines. A first-time visitor is not the owner and does not know what these proposals are, so the link is noise or confusing.
findings.source: Header: "Owner view: proposals waiting for your decision."

findings.text: The next steps are concrete: prerequisites, clone, run setup.sh, then a sample command. The header links to them, so a newcomer who knows what they want can find the next step fast.
findings.source: Next steps: "Get the code: git clone https://github.com/doodla/athena.git" ... "Try it with a one-line request: athena ask \"add a changelog\""

findings.text: Several glossary entries say the term is undefined. This is honest, but a newcomer still has to read words like endpoint, wake and heartbeat without knowing what they mean.
findings.source: Glossary: "The firstmate source does not define a durable record." / "The firstmate source does not define an endpoint." / "The firstmate source does not define a wake."

findings.text: Defining the key terms (captain, yolo, green, red) before using them, then following one piece of work start to finish, makes the firstmate content easier to follow than its size suggests.
The closing section describes how the page is built inside the repository. That is useful to maintainers but means nothing to a first-time visitor.
findings.source: About this page: "the name of the folder under studies/ that holds the data this page is generated from."
